title: The Concept of Bad Faith in Modern Thought
text:
In existential philosophy, the notion of 'bad faith' describes a mechanism by which individuals deceive themselves regarding their radical freedom. It involves denying one's autonomy by adopting roles or assumptions that suggest an inherent essence or predefined nature, rather than recognizing that existence precedes essence.

This self-deception often manifests as an attempt to escape responsibility for defining oneself. Instead of confronting the anguish of absolute freedom, a person operating in bad faith treats themselves as an object determined by external forces—such as social expectations, institutional roles, or biological imperatives.
